At-Risk Populations
As stated previously, it would be a daunting task to acquire a
working knowledge of all potential drug-nutrient interactions.
However, a study of the basic principles of pharmacology and 
categories of interactions reveals that certain situations place
individuals at risk. Th ese may include disease state, organ func-
tion, or treatment modality. Furthermore, certain groups of 
individuals are more likely than others, not only to take more 
medications, but to also have an increased risk of improper or
inadequate pharmacokinetics. Knowing these populations are 
at risk allows the practitioner to target them for monitoring and
education.
